naming: The loader reads the document with YamlDotNet's CamelCaseNamingConvention and refuses any key it does not know.

keys.description: Always mapping: this document fills one OSDU template.
The mapping's name. With version it makes the reference Name@version a delivery flow pins under render.mapping, and the file is mappings/Name@version.yaml.
The mapping's version. It is part of the reference Name@version and of every rendered record's render context, so a new version re-renders the records that use it.
Free text describing what the mapping delivers.
The saved template version the mapping fills. A run refuses to render against any other, and one the catalog does not hold stops the run.
The OSDU kind of the records the mapping renders, authority:source:entityType:major.minor.patch, such as osdu:wks:work-product-component--WellLog:1.4.0.
The saved template version: the 16 hexadecimal characters the Templates page and 'sqlflow template list' show for the kind.
The rows the mapping renders: the source system, the key the delivery key and the OSDU id are derived from, and what identifies a record to a person.
The source system. It enters the delivery key, and so the OSDU id: two mappings that deliver the same rows into the same entity type and partition need different systems or keys.

The columns of the dataset's own row that identify a record, in order, each named as it is (log_id). The delivery key, and so the OSDU id, is derived from them; a key column need not be written into the record.
A key column, named as it is, such as log_id.

Optional display text for the ledger and the GUI, with {<column>} tokens naming columns of the dataset's own row, such as "{wellbore_uwi} / {log_id}", cut at 400 characters. It never enters the record.

Optional columns of the dataset's own row whose values identify the record to a person (a wellbore id, a log id), each named as it is. The ledger indexes every value, so the Records page finds the record by any of them. Search only: never in the record.
An identifying column, named as it is, such as wellbore_uwi.
Values the flow supplies under render.parameters, each declared here. dataPartition is always declared, and a flow value for a parameter the mapping does not declare is refused.
One parameter, read in a literal's text and in an id template as {$param.<name>}.
True when the flow has to supply the parameter (or it has a default).
The value used when the flow supplies none. It is mapping content and is not expanded as a reference.
Free text describing the parameter.
The record sets the mapping's $search nodes look in on the platform, as each record needs one, rather than capturing them into the cache. One search per kind, each read by a node.
One search, read by a node as $search: <name>.
The kind searched: one entity type, at one version or every version, such as osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:*.
The saved template whose schema says how the searched kind's properties are indexed, so a $findBy line is asked the way the platform answers it.
The kind of the saved template, such as osdu:wks:master-data--Wellbore:1.3.0.
The saved template version: 16 hexadecimal characters.
Free text describing the search.

The record the mapping renders, laid out the way the rendered record is: acl, legal, tags and data, and the properties below them. Every word of the mapping language starts with '$' ($from, $forEach...); every other key is a property of the record, so no template's property name is ever read as the language. A property that is not written is left out of the record.

A property of the record, written as one of four nodes. A literal is the value it is: text, a number, a boolean or a list, such as ReferenceCurveID: MD. Its text reads a parameter as {$param.<name>} and no other token. An object is a map of the property names it holds, each a node in turn. A value node is a map whose keys all start with '$'. It reads one value with $from: <column>, $expr: <expression>, $value: <literal>, $cache: <Type>.<field> or $search: <name>, and takes beside it $findBy (with $cache and $search: one line or a list of <field> = <column> or <field> = 'text', tried in order), $modifiers (a list applied top to bottom: trim, upper, lower, split: { separator, part }, replace: { <value>: <value or ~> } with otherwise beside it, or replace: $cache.<Type> with match, field and otherwise beside it, equals: <text>, date or date: <format>, number or number: { decimal, group }, id: "<template>", or ref, ref: <Entity> or ref: <group>--<Entity>, the reference {$param.dataPartition}:<group>--<Entity>:{$value}: to the record whose code is the value, of the type the property points to; id or ref is always the last), $when (a condition: an expression giving true or false, such as log_status = "FINAL" or not empty(curve_unit); false leaves the property out), $required (true by default: an empty value holds the record; false leaves the property out), $ignoreSeparators (with $cache) and $description. A $forEach node repeats the rows of a child dataset as the items of an array: $forEach: <child dataset>, and $item laying out the properties each row fills, with $where (a condition each child row must hold to become an item), $when (decides for the whole array), $required and $description. A bare column name reads the row the node is in: the dataset's own row, or under $forEach the item's row; $dataset.<column> reads the dataset's own row from anywhere. An id template reads {$value}, {<column>}, {$dataset.<column>}, {$cache.<Type>.<field>} and {$param.<name>}. A property whose own name starts with '$' is written with one more, $$<name>; what $value holds is written verbatim. An expression reads a column by its name (in backticks when the name is a keyword, starts with a digit or holds '-'), $dataset.<column> and $param.<name>, and writes text in quotes; it compares with =, !=, <, <=, >, >= and in [ ... ], joins conditions with and, or and not, joins text with &, computes with + - * /, and calls iif(condition, value, other), coalesce(value, value, ...), nullif(value, other), empty(value), trim(text), upper(text), lower(text), substring(text, start, length), left(text, count), right(text, count), replace(text, find, with), length(text), contains(text, part), startsWith(text, part), endsWith(text, part), number(value), text(value), round(number, digits) and abs(number). Text compares ignoring case and surrounding spaces; no value is the same only as no value; arithmetic on no value gives no value.

The access control list every OSDU record carries: owners and viewers, each a literal list of at least one entitlements group, such as owners: ["{$param.aclOwner}"]. A DSPDM business object row has none.

The legal block every OSDU record carries: legaltags and otherRelevantDataCountries, each a literal list of at least one value, free of repeats, such as legaltags: ["{$param.legalTag}"] and otherRelevantDataCountries: [NO]. A DSPDM business object row has none.
Free keys of the record, each a text: a literal, such as DeliveredBy: osdu-delivery, or a value node, such as SourceProject: { $from: source_project }.

The record's data, laid out as the template names its properties: each a literal, an object of properties, a value node ($from, $expr, $value, $cache or $search with its settings) or a $forEach array whose $item lays out what each row of a child dataset fills.
What every fixture renders with unless it says otherwise, written once rather than in each fixture.
The render parameters every fixture renders with; a fixture's own parameters replace them name by name.
A parameter's value.
Example rows and the exact record each must render to under the pinned template and cache. The preflight gate renders them before every run: the mapping's regression suite.
One fixture: a row, the parameters and search answers it renders with, and the record it must render to.
What the fixture shows.
The render parameters the fixture renders with, over fixtureDefaults.parameters.
A parameter's value.
The dataset's row: its columns and values.
A column's value.
Child dataset rows, by child dataset name.
The rows of one child dataset.
One child row: its columns and values.
A column's value.
What the platform is assumed to answer to each search the render asks; a fixture never asks it.
One answer the platform is assumed to give: the search, the property and value asked for, and the record found.
The search, by its name under searches.
The property the findBy line compares, such as data.FacilityName.
The value asked for.
The one record found; left out when the platform holds no such record.
The exact record the row renders to, as JSON, compared canonically.
